schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    USER_ID INT,
    SESSION_ID INT,
    ACTIVITY_DATE DATE,
    ACTIVITY_TYPE ENUM('OPEN_SESSION', 'END_SESSION', 'SCROLL_DOWN', 'SEND_MESSAGE'),
    CHECK (ACTIVITY_TYPE IN ('OPEN_SESSION', 'END_SESSION', 'SCROLL_DOWN', 'SEND_MESSAGE'))
);
q1: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE ACTIVITY_DATE BETWEEN '2019-06-28' AND '2019-07-27' GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
q2: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE ACTIVITY_DATE > DATE_SUB('2019-07-27', INTERVAL 30 DAY) GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE ACTIVITY_DATE BETWEEN '2019-06-28' AND '2019-07-27' GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE ACTIVITY_DATE > DATE_SUB('2019-07-27', INTERVAL 30 DAY) GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 explicitly filters records where ACTIVITY_DATE is between '2019-06-28' and '2019-07-27' (inclusive). Q2 filters records where ACTIVITY_DATE is greater than a date computed as 30 days before '2019-07-27', which is '2019-06-27'. This means Q2 includes dates from '2019-06-28' to '2019-07-27' as well as any dates beyond '2019-07-27'. Therefore, Q2 may include more dates than Q1, depending on the data, leading to different results.
counterexample_dsp: Create a test database where there are activity records on '2019-07-28'. Q1 will exclude this date, while Q2 will include it, leading to different results.
